summary: A complaint from a Lincoln Laboratory author about the stream of questionnaires reaching ARPANET sites, especially the seven-page NCP survey of RFC 460, which gave no explanation and a two-week deadline. It asks questionnaire senders to think about the time they ask for. It is an opinion piece, not a protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 459 objects to the number of questionnaires being sent to network sites. The author says that filling them out takes time, especially when the questions do not apply, and asks senders to explain their purpose and consider the workload.

subtitle: A complaint about the time that repeated network questionnaires required from sites.

tldr.problem: The author says network sites were receiving a steady stream of questionnaires that distracted people from other work.
tldr.mechanism: The note points to the seven-page NCP questionnaire in RFC 460, which gave no explanation for the request and asked for a response in two weeks.
tldr.outcome: RFC 459 is an opinion note asking questionnaire senders to consider the time and limited staff available at recipient sites.

sections.title: A Stream of Questionnaires
sections.content: W. Kantrowitz of LL-TX-2 says a steady stream of questionnaires had been arriving from the network community. Each one took attention away from other work and increased annoyance. The seven-page NCP questionnaire in RFC 460 pushed the author's frustration over the top.
sections.plainLanguage: The author says network sites were receiving many questionnaires, and the latest one was especially long. Each request took time away from other work.

sections.title: The Cost of Answering
sections.content:
The author notes that a careful response takes time, especially when questions apply only partly to the person answering. The memo objects that RFC 460 offers no explanation for its questionnaire's purpose and asks for a response within two weeks.

The author also criticizes the promise of more questionnaires. The concern is that requests should account for the work required at the sites asked to respond.
sections.plainLanguage: Answering a questionnaire carefully takes time, and some questions may not apply. The author asks senders to explain why they need the information and allow for the effort involved.

sections.title: A Request to Consider Site Workloads
sections.content:
The note ends by asking people who create questionnaires and other meta-work to remember that some network sites have limited staff and other responsibilities. The author argues that repeated requests can prevent those sites from getting their work done.

The RFC is an opinion note about the burden of questionnaires; it does not define a network protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks questionnaire senders to consider that recipient sites have limited staff and other work to do. The note expresses an opinion and specifies no protocol.
